## Summary

Recorded a user release ruling that binds both live initiatives: do not publish a new sofar.sh until commit-attribution is finished — let the whole thing land, then publish once. Filed as an operational fact rather than a decision, per this repo's own classification of release commands, as commit-attribution M7, and named in the hand-written .sofar/repo.md so it renders in EVERY session's digest rather than only in one record's — which matters because any session could stage a release. The reasoning kept with it: attribution is a chain (hook writes the trailer, core/attribution.ts reads it, doctor reports whether it works, the shipping notice and review packet consume it), so a partial release puts users in the worst available state — a hook writing trailers nothing consumes, or a doctor reporting attribution off in a version with no way to switch it on. Two consequences recorded with it: the prepare-commit-msg hook stays uninstalled in this repo until the release, since an accurate "attribution off" beats a misleading "installed but nothing attributed"; and this initiative's own protocol-block change rides the same release, because protocol blocks are a versioned ledger and a half-shipped one leaves repos matching no known version. Peers moved both initiatives while this ran: commit-attribution is 16 done with 6 remaining, session-orientation 3/8 with Phase 1 complete.
